title: Loop through a list
hook: Do something to every item in a list, then total it and rank it.

warmup.explain: Spots count from 0. Spot 0 is a, spot 1 is b.
range starts at the first number and stops just before the last. 1, 2, 3.

warmup.q: `age = input("Age? ")`. What type of thing is `age`?
warmup.explain: input always gives text, even if you type digits. That is why we use int() to convert.

why.heading: A list is made for looping
why.text: A shot list is not for staring at. You go down it, one shot at a time. A Python list works the same way, and you already know the tool that repeats things: **for**.

why.heading: for item in list
why.text:
`for shot in shots:`

This means: take the items one at a time, call the current one `shot`, and run the indented lines. You pick the name `shot`. Make it a singular word for the list name: `crew` and `person`, `rates` and `rate`.

why.heading: Maths on a whole list
why.text:
Python has ready-made tools for number lists:

`sum(rates)` adds them all up.
`max(rates)` finds the biggest.
`min(rates)` finds the smallest.

No running total needed. One line each.

why.heading: Sort a copy
why.text: `sorted(rates)` gives a new list in order, smallest first. Words go A to Z. Your original list stays as it was, so nothing is lost.

why.heading: Numbered lists
why.text:
Want 1, 2, 3 next to each item? Use `enumerate`:

`for n, shot in enumerate(shots, 1):`

It hands you a number `n` and the item together. The `1` says start counting at 1. Copy this shape and it just works.

watch.intro: Tap Run. A list of day rates in rand, looped, totalled and ranked.
watch.code:
rates = [850, 1200, 950]
for r in rates:
    print("Rate:", r)
print("Total", sum(rates))
print("Top", max(rates))
for n, r in enumerate(sorted(rates), 1):
    print(n, r)
explain: The first `for` prints every rate, in list order.
`sum` and `max` do the whole list in one go.
`sorted` puts the rates smallest first, and `enumerate` numbers them from 1.
The indented lines belong to the loop. The unindented lines run once, after it.
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: remove the 4 spaces in front of the first `print("Rate:", r)` line and tap Run. The error says `IndentationError: expected an indented block`. A loop needs its lines indented. Put the spaces back.

tasks.title: Roll call
tasks.task:
Say hi to everyone on the crew with a loop. It must show:

`Hi, Sam`
`Hi, Thandi`
`Hi, Lebo`
tasks.starter:
crew = ["Sam", "Thandi", "Lebo"]
# loop through crew and say hi
hints: Start with: for name in crew:
Indent the next line by 4 spaces and print the greeting using name.
print("Hi,", name) shows Hi, then the name with a space between.

tests.expect:
Hi, Sam
Hi, Thandi
Hi, Lebo

tasks.title: Day rate totals
tasks.task:
These are four crew day rates in rand. Print the total, the highest and the lowest:

`Total: R4450`
`Highest: R1500`
`Lowest: R800`
tasks.starter:
rates = [1200, 950, 1500, 800]
# print the total, highest and lowest
tasks.solution:
rates = [1200, 950, 1500, 800]
print(f"Total: R{sum(rates)}")
print(f"Highest: R{max(rates)}")
print(f"Lowest: R{min(rates)}")
hints: Python already has sum(), max() and min() for this. No loop needed.
Put them inside an f-string, like f"Total: R{sum(rates)}"
Do the same for max(rates) and min(rates), one print line each.

tests.expect:
Total: R4450
Highest: R1500
Lowest: R800

tasks.title: Ranked run paces
tasks.task:
These are pace times for four runs, in minutes per km. Print them fastest (smallest) first, numbered from 1:

`1. 5.2 min/km`
`2. 5.4 min/km`
`3. 5.8 min/km`
`4. 6.1 min/km`
hints: You need sorted(paces) to order them, and enumerate(..., 1) to number them.
The shape is: for n, p in enumerate(sorted(paces), 1):

recap: `for item in mylist:` runs the indented lines once per item.
`sum`, `min`, `max` do maths on a whole number list.

words.meaning: The name that holds the current item, like shot in for shot in shots.
Adds up all the numbers in a list.
Gives a new list in order. The original stays.
Pairs each item with a counting number.
